coverage.reason: States the fund 'can deliver low-basis securities in kind rather than selling them for cash' and that under IRC §852(b)(6) 'a RIC recognizes no gain on that in-kind distribution.'

Says the fund 'can purge its most appreciated lots without realizing gains,' which reduces embedded gains, and contrasts this with mutual funds whose cash-redemption sales 'can generate capital gain distributions passed to all remaining shareholders.'

Says 'Your own sale of ETF shares is still taxable,' that the result is 'deferral, not permanent,' and that cash redemptions and rebalancing or index-change sales 'can still realize gains,' so distributions are not ruled out.

rationale: The answer meets all three required minimums: fund-level nonrecognition on in-kind transfers, removal of low-basis lots reducing distributions versus cash-redeeming funds, and clear limits (no absolute exemption, investor sale taxable, deferral only, depends on in-kind transactions). It contains no central error and no material local falsehood.
